newsitem.title: USA: Group claims L.A. oil terminals break U.S. air law.
newsitem.headline: Group claims L.A. oil terminals break U.S. air law.

text.p: LOS ANGELES, July 24 (Reute) - A California-based environmental group is demanding that five large oil companies install vapor-removing equipment at their tanker terminals in the Los Angeles Harbor.

In a suit filed Wednesday, Communities for a Better Environment (CBE) alleges that Chevron Corp Tosco Corp, Unocal Corp, GATX Corp, and Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp, are violating part of the U.S Federal Clean Air Act by allowing toxic vapors from gasoline and oil tankers to escape into neighboring communities.
"There is no smoking gun relationship...but you use common sense by noting what you see and hear in the communites," said Carlos Porras, a spokesman for the group's southern California chapter.
He claimed the group will bring data to court showing respiratory problems, rashes, and dizziness were caused by the vapors.
Company officials say vapors never or rarely exceed federal standards and that they actually remove more harmful fumes from the air under a government "pollution trading" program.

The program, administered by the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD), allows California businesses to buy and scrap old, higher-polluting cars in return for more emissions permitted from their overall operations.
"The air is cleaner because we've taken cars off the road," said Carolyn Green, director of Government and public affairs for Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (UDS) Corp.
Company officials, who could not comment on specific charges, say the CBE's case is without merit
CBE says the program ends up concentrating pollution in the Los Angeles harbor area, home to large concentration of minorities.

CBE is simultaneously filing a federal civil right complaint against SCAQMD and California Air Resource Board (CARB). The complaint will be reviewed by the agencies' overseer, the U.S Environmental Proctection Agency.
